## Added

- **Dangling file references are flagged.** If `proposal.md`'s `## Files This Change Will Touch`
  contract names a file that doesn't exist and isn't marked `(new)`, the gate now says so —
  `scope refs: DANGLING …` in the panel, and a **Scope** section in the compiled review document
  lists it. It warns, it never blocks.

- **Mark files the change will create with `(new)`.** The contract already listed existing files and
  new files together; a trailing `(new)` (e.g. `- src/lib/thing.ts (new)`) is what tells the two
  apart. An unmarked path still means "this file already exists", which is what the dangling check
  relies on. The Propose turn is told to write them this way.

- **Scope is re-checked after implementation.** The gate's scope check runs before Execute, so it
  only ever saw what Propose changed — not what Execute actually touched. A file changed outside the
  contract during Execute is now named at the **Archive now?** prompt (and logged to `CONTEXT.md`).

## Changed

- **Planning phases compact their context at every boundary**, not just before Execute: after
  grilling and before **Explore**, and after Explore and before **Propose**. Everything each phase
  relies on is already on disk (the brainstorm, `EXPLORATION.md`), so this cuts prep-phase token cost
  with no correctness trade-off — prep was the largest single cost centre in the last benchmark.

## Fixed

- **Scope contracts no longer drop non-JS paths.** The parser only accepted a hard-coded directory
  or JS/MD/YAML extension whitelist and only stripped commentary after ` -- `, so `app/handler.go`,
  `packages/core/index.ts`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `Makefile`, and any path with other trailing
  commentary never entered the contract. Those files were then reported OUT OF SCOPE once Execute
  touched them, and the dangling check never saw them. The path is now the first token and the rest
  is commentary, whatever the separator. Extensionless names inside a directory
  (`bin/readyset-flow`, `scripts/deploy`) are accepted too.

## Install / Update

```
npx readyset-flow install
npx readyset-flow update
```
or with `bunx` in place of `npx`.

The extension module is referenced in place, so updating the package is enough — no re-install
needed.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/fresp/readyset-flow/compare/0.12.1...0.13.0
